cultural.vision_reason: This is a Mughal-style Indian miniature portrait of a named governor of Kabul, painted in classic Mughal court style with floral border decoration — this is Indian/Mughal painting tradition, unrelated to the Afar people of the Horn of Africa.

physical.title: album; painting
physical.summary:
Portrait of Saʿíd Xán Bahádur Ẓafar Jang; single-page painting mounted on a detached album folio. The governer of Kabul stands in profile wearing a green tunic and carrying a dagger, sword and shield. Blue ground with cottony white clouds. Flowering plants along lower edge. Framed by pink border with gold floral motifs; margin decorated with motif of alternating pink and red flowering plants outlined in gold against neutral ground; entire folio bordered by a thin, green adhesive strip. Inscribed. Folio belongs to a series of single-page paintings and drawings of Indian rulers, all of which were once attached to the leaves of the album 1920,0917,0.13, also housed in the British Museum collection.
Ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a European Baroque etching depicting the Siege of Limerick during the Williamite War in Ireland, showing King William III with advisors before a map, troops, and cannon fire—a Dutch print by Pickaert/Schoonebeek after Romeyn de Hooghe, illustrating European history. It has no connection whatsoever to the Afar people of the Horn of Africa; it is European fine art depicting a European historical/military scene.

physical.title: print; book-illustration
physical.summary:
Siege of Limerick by the armies of William III; the new King of England seen in the right foreground with his war advisors talking in front of a military map; cannon firing in the background and city of Limerick seen from afar. Plate 21 of 24 in Gregorio Leti's 'Prodigio Della Natura' containing 24 book-illustrations etched by Pieter Pickaert and Adriaen Schoonebeek, originally published by Adriaen Schoonebeek; some etchings after Romeyn de Hooghe (Amsterdam: Gregorio Leti, 1695).  1695
Etching
